title: Build turns every Monitor and Not OK finding into a work order line
preconditions:
1. The organisation has ShopCoach.
2. A completed inspection has Monitor and Not OK findings (Work Order Lines — Create & Edit (+ Work Orders — Create & Edit to create a new work order). Building requires ShopCoach (S2-R0).).
steps:
1. Start a build from the completed inspection.
2. Choose a target work order.
3. Add the lines and inspect them.
expected:
1. Every Monitor and Not OK finding is represented by at least one line; ShopCoach composes each line's name, description, time estimate and parts (the label, measured value and note are inputs, not the line text — see S15).
2. A generated line behaves as an ordinary work order line from that point on, indistinguishable from a typed one.
3. When added, lines arrive approved or awaiting authorisation per the shop's existing auto-approve setting, exactly as a manually added line does; an Approved work order needs no re-approval (approval applies to lines).
4. Generated lines resolve labour type as the manual New Line form does (default, else first available), and the rate follows the labour type; the ShopCoach time estimate is carried and editable, defaulting to zero where none is proposed.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8181 and story SV-9100 (S2, Turn findings into work order lines) and the Digital Inspections V2 specification version 18, sections S2-R1, S2-R2, S2-R7, S2-R8, S2-R9, S2-R10, read on 21 August 2026.

title: Target work order chosen up front; closed WO forces a new one
preconditions:
1. ShopCoach present; a completed inspection with findings.
2. You can reach an inspection whose WO is open and one whose WO is closed.
steps:
1. Start a build where the inspection's WO is open; observe the target choice.
2. Start a build where the inspection's WO is closed.
3. Observe the new-WO customer/asset.
expected:
1. The user chooses the target before any drafting starts: the work order the inspection was run on, or a new work order.
2. The existing work order is offered only while open (Estimate, Approved, In Progress or Review).
3. When the WO the inspection was run on is closed (Complete, Invoiced, Paid, or an invoice exists), the system creates a new work order without asking.
4. A new work order is created for the same customer and asset as the original, using their current values.
5. A closed work order is never modified — the system creates a new one instead.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8181 and story SV-9100 (S2, Turn findings into work order lines) and the Digital Inspections V2 specification version 18, sections S2-R3, S2-R4, S2-R5, S2-R6, read on 21 August 2026.

title: Navigation precedes drafting; state changes only on Add Lines
preconditions: 1. ShopCoach present; a completed inspection with findings.
steps:
1. Choose the target and observe navigation vs drafting timing.
2. Watch the lines draft on the Lines tab.

3. If lines were already added from this inspection, the user is asked to confirm before adding a second set; the check is made when Add Lines is pressed, on the state at that moment.

title: Build negatives: no ShopCoach, not completed, no findings, permission gates
preconditions:
1. You can reach inspections that are not completed, have no findings, and orgs with/without ShopCoach.
2. Users with and without WO-Lines and WO-Create rights, and without See Financial Data.

1. Try to build without ShopCoach.
2. Try on a not-completed inspection and one with no Monitor/Not OK findings.
3. As a user without WO Lines — Create & Edit; then without WO — Create & Edit; then without See Financial Data.
expected:
1. Building requires ShopCoach: without it the completed inspection offers only the report and a link to its work order, and no build action at all.
2. If the inspection is not completed, or has no Monitor/Not OK findings, the build is not offered.
3. Without WO Lines — Create & Edit the build is unavailable from any entry point.
4. Without WO — Create & Edit the create-new-work-order option is not shown; only add-lines-to-the-open-WO is offered.
5. Without See Financial Data the build is still allowed; money on the resulting work order stays hidden by the existing rules.

---

title: Build edge cases: closed-by-another, deleted WO, concurrent, no labour types
preconditions: 1. ShopCoach present; inspections whose WOs can change state mid-flow.
steps:
1. Choose add-lines-to-open-WO, then have someone close it, then confirm.
2. Delete the original WO before confirming.
3. Have two users draft from the same inspection at once.
4. Build with a shop that has no labour types; delete a built WO afterward; reverse an invoice.
expected:
1. If the chosen open WO was closed by someone else meanwhile, the system tells the user and creates nothing.
2. If the original WO is deleted before confirm, the build fails without creating a partial result.
3. Two users drafting at once duplicate nothing by drafting (a draft is not a WO line); duplication happens only if both press Add Lines, which is accepted and recoverable.
4. With no labour types the build proceeds and labour cost is zero.
5. If a built work order is later deleted, the inspection counts as needing a work order again; reversing an invoice does not change the inspection's state.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8181 and story SV-9100 (S2, Turn findings into work order lines) and the Digital Inspections V2 specification version 18, sections S2-E3..E10, read on 21 August 2026.

title: ShopCoach brief is composed from the inspection; user never types a prompt
preconditions: 1. The org has ShopCoach; the S2 conditions are met; the user has chosen the target.
steps:
1. Start a build and observe whether any prompt/query box appears.
2. Inspect (via the brief contract) what each finding contributes.
3. Check a per-axle finding's traceability.
expected:
1. The system composes the brief from the inspection itself: for each Monitor and Not OK finding it includes the field label, its section, the measured value and unit, the verdict, and the technician's note.
2. A per-axle finding names its axle and measurement row, so a proposed line traces back to the measurement that caused it.
3. The brief states what ShopCoach may not do: invent a part it was not given, turn a passing finding into a line, or leave a flagged finding unrepresented.
4. The user never types anything to get lines — no prompt, no query box, no configuration step anywhere in the flow.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8181 and story SV-9404 (S15, Draft the lines with ShopCoach) and the Digital Inspections V2 specification version 18, sections S15-R1, S15-R2, S15-R3, S15-R4, read on 21 August 2026.

title: ShopCoach failure and empty-result are stated plainly; nothing added
preconditions: 1. ShopCoach present; the call can return no lines or fail.
steps:
1. Trigger a build where ShopCoach returns no lines.
2. Trigger a build where the ShopCoach call fails.
3. Navigate away mid-draft.
4. Build a finding with an empty note.
expected:
1. If ShopCoach returns no lines at all, the user is told so plainly and the work order is unchanged.
2. If the call fails, the user is told it failed — an empty panel is not acceptable, because there is no non-AI path to fall back to.
3. If the user navigates away while drafting runs, nothing is added.
4. A passing finding never becomes a proposed line; no part is proposed that ShopCoach was not given.
5. A finding with an empty note is still sent and still represented — an empty note is not a reason to drop it.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8181 and story SV-9404 (S15, Draft the lines with ShopCoach) and the Digital Inspections V2 specification version 18, sections S15-N2, S15-N3, S15-E1..E4, read on 21 August 2026.
